statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains at 24 as confirmed U.S. strikes on three Iranian crude oil tankers and Iranian missile attacks on two U.S. Navy ships increase reopening-gap sensitivity, while the weekend NQ closure prevents live confirmation of persistent one-way Nasdaq structure.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH; Tail remains below the block threshold. Stress is extreme from the confirmed U.S.-Iran military exchange, energy disruption and Friday's higher-rate repricing, with no live NQ path available during the weekend closure.
headline: Confirmed tanker strikes keep weekend Nasdaq regime at WATCH
body: NQ is closed. Reuters reports U.S. forces struck three Iranian crude oil tankers after Iranian missile attacks on two U.S. Navy ships. Friday's stronger jobs report lifted yields and pressured equities; fresh shared Finviz context shows strong semiconductors but weaker megacaps and is used only as supplementary latest-session evidence.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours span Friday's post-payroll repricing, two brief orange Tail episodes during live trading, the transition into weekend closure, and the move back to WATCH after Gulf escalation. Since NQ closed, elevated Tail has reflected discontinuity and reopening risk rather than observed persistent mean-reversion failure.
outlookSummary: NQ remains closed throughout this 24-hour horizon. If no additional verified U.S.-Iran escalation or material Hormuz disruption occurs, Tail is projected to ease within WATCH as the tanker-strike shock ages; Stress remains extreme from conflict, energy costs and rate pressure while confidence declines as Friday's tradable evidence becomes older.
